objective: RULER-FLAT-20261111-001 direction 1 (G1, question 9), at the owner's go-ahead of 2026-11-11 (overlapping bases: a knot may meet any number of others): read bases with no limit on how many knots a pair lies in under the not-all-equal law, and catalogue what the law makes that no knot names: emergent knots, ties and frozen distinctions, the smallest knot configurations that force them, and the compressed base they form. Families: every connected configuration of at most 6 knots; every base on 4 to 6 distinctions and random bases on 7 to 10; NAE-SURFACE's 822 swap-made bases (160 faithful) and GROW-COUNT's grown bases re-read as objects; bases in which every co-knotted pair lies in exactly three knots. Standalone value relative to the nearest known work: the Pasch configuration and the 2-colourings of triple systems are classical; a catalogue of what proper 2-colourings force on triples outside the system was not found.
stop_rule: One registered census, the four lemmas proved and refereed, one referee pass over the census; report and hold.
title: What not-all-equal makes of overlapping bases
